//: Every threshold the ingestion pipeline uses to decide what is worth acting on.
These are operational policy, not physics: what counts as 'too much fuel to have evaporated'
or 'a battery too flat to ride out an outage' depends on the fleet, the hardware and how much
false-positive noise the NOC will tolerate. Tune them here. Every value is validated at
startup — a nonsensical setting stops the app with a readable message rather than quietly
producing an anomalies page nobody can trust.
Any key omitted here falls back to the documented default in code.

DecisionEngine.//: Filters applied to the AI analyzer's output before it becomes an alert or optimization.

//: How a reported measurement converts to a percentage. These describe YOUR hardware and YOUR
network plan. A 48 V window applied to a 24 V battery bank reports every healthy battery as
flat, so get these right before tuning the anomaly rules that read them.

Rsrp.//: dBm window mapped onto 0-100% signal. Defaults are the usual LTE/NR planning range.

Battery.//: DC bus voltage window mapped onto 0-100% state of charge. Defaults describe a 48 V string.

HealthScore.//: Where the provider's own health score crosses into warning/critical, absent any open alarm.

SnapshotAnomalies.//: The five rules derived from a site's reported plant state. Each can be switched off.

//: Fuel that left a tank the generator was not running to burn. Set DropPoints above the
noise floor of your level senders (floats typically wobble 1-3 points) or the rule will
cry theft at every tanker bounce.

GeneratorOveruse.//: Generator running while commercial power is available — burning diesel the grid could carry.

BatteryDegrade.//: State of charge, measured against the Battery calibration window above.

//: A site that has stopped speaking. Keep StaleMinutes comfortably above your feed's polling
interval — a 15-minute feed is always a few minutes stale, and a threshold below the
interval would flag every healthy site in the fleet.
Straight-line projection of the tank running dry, from the burn rate between the last two
readings. Set WarningHours to your realistic refuelling lead time — a warning that arrives
after the truck could no longer have got there is a postmortem, not a warning.
